subject: Orion Labs — procurement path, trial success criteria, billing start
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Holt <samantha@orionlabs.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: procurement path, trial success criteria, billing start

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Summary of what we covered:
- Goal: run a 30-day pilot of Redwood inference across two services (ingestion pipeline + conversational endpoint) and validate latency and cost per 1k tokens.
- Success criteria: sustained >8k tokens/day across both services, average p95 latency <350ms, and integration of prefix caching in staging.
- Procurement options discussed: corporate card to start immediately vs. PO (finance-driven) vs. AWS Marketplace listing (favored by procurement for consolidated billing).

Open items / asks from Orion: 
1) Procurement preference (card vs PO vs marketplace) and estimated PO lead time.
2) Confirmation of start date for trial and any billing constraints (do you want billing to start automatically after trial thresholds are met?).
3) Any legal/contractual must-haves (data residency, NDA touchpoints, security docs).

Proposed next steps: 
- I attached a short SOW draft and our W-9 to accelerate PO. (Attachment: Orion_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf, W-9_Redwood_Inc.pdf)
- Option A (fast path): start trial on Sep 6 on corporate card — we enable production keys, billing would begin if usage exceeds your defined threshold. Good if you want to validate quickly.
- Option B (procurement path): Redwood sends SOW & invoice once PO is received; billing start can be set to the agreed start date in the PO (we typically see a 10–15 business day procurement lead time).
- Parallel path: we can also work with AWS Marketplace — if your procurement team prefers that, we can introduce Marketplace pricing packaging and start contracting in parallel.

Please confirm which option you prefer and the name/email of your procurement contact so we can loop them in. If PO, please share estimated lead time and any PO template.

Thanks — I’ll pause any auto-activation until we get your preference.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: Orion_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf (proposal, 2 pages), W-9_Redwood_Inc.pdf

From: Samantha Holt <samantha@orionlabs.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Vargas <diego@orionlabs.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: procurement path, trial success criteria, billing start

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the clear recap. Orion prefers to go via PO if possible — finance requires the SOW attached to a PO and they also need our vendors to provide a W-9 and current SOC 2 report. Estimated procurement lead time is ~10 business days once we have the SOW + W-9.

A few notes/questions from finance and security: 
- Marketplace: our procurement team prefers AWS Marketplace for standardized billing, but they need a marketplace SKU/pricing bundle from your side. Is that something Redwood can provide while we process the PO?
- Billing start: finance is generally okay with start dates specified on the PO. Given the internal calendar, our target for live billing would be Sep 20 if we follow the PO route.
- Contacts: Diego Vargas (diego@orionlabs.com) will own procurement. Please send any invoice templates, your vendor contact for PO questions, and a link to your SOC 2 report.

Samantha
Samantha Holt
VP Product, Orion Labs
samantha@orionlabs.com

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: procurement path, trial success criteria, billing start

Hi Samantha (and Diego) —

Appreciate the quick reply and thanks for the clarity on sequencing. We can support both paths — here’s a pragmatic plan to keep momentum: 

1) Parallel tracks: 
  - Procurement (preferred by you): I will update the SOW with the minimal contractual terms and send to Diego for PO processing. If PO is issued, we’ll target billing start Sep 20 per your note.
  - Fast validation (optional): If you want to accelerate technical validation we can provision a trial with a corporate card on Sep 6 and mark billing to be enabled only if your defined usage threshold is crossed. This would allow your engineers to validate latency/cost while procurement runs.

2) Marketplace: we can provide a Marketplace SKU/pricing bundle — I’ll coordinate with our partnerships team and share a one-page SKU/pricing doc by COB Mon Aug 31. That allows your procurement to compare Marketplace vs direct PO pricing.

3) Docs: attaching W-9 (attached earlier) and a link to our SOC 2 summary: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-summary (public summary; full report available upon NDA).

Lauren — looping you in to confirm a 7-business-day turnaround on minimal SOW redlines (indemnity, data residency note) if Diego needs changes. Monica — can you prepare a short onboarding checklist for the trial path (keys, staging endpoints, token budget monitoring)?

If we proceed with the PO path, Diego — could you confirm the PO template and anticipated signatory and whether your legal team needs a draft contract?

Thanks,
Marcus

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Orion Labs PO path — legal quick review request

Lauren / Monica —

Looping you both in for a fast legal + onboarding check. Samantha from Orion confirmed PO preference and indicated a Sep 20 target for billing start if PO route is taken. Diego Vargas is procurement contact.

Action items I need within 48 hours: 
- Lauren: quick pass on the attached SOW draft with prioritized redlines. Goal is to keep the SOW minimal so finance can process quickly. Key asks from Orion: indemnity wording, data residency note, and explicit billing start date field. Can we accept their standard PO with our SOW attached? If not, what minimal changes do we need?
- Monica: onboarding checklist (keys, staging endpoint, token budget alerts, success-metric dashboard) so we can attach to the SOW and shorten procurement questions. Also estimate how long it will take to provision trial access if they want Sep 6 (fast path).

I attached the current SOW and our W-9 in the thread. Also flagging that marketplace SKU/pricing will be provided by Monday — might help accelerate procurement.

If legal needs more time, suggest we propose the fast-path card option to start on Sep 6 and switch to PO billing on Sep 20. Please advise on any gating items that would block PO issuance.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — I’ll be on call tomorrow afternoon if you want to triage.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
